verdict_reason: The promoted kernel is the Grassberger-Procaccia estimator read in the SCALING REGION, which is what GP 1983 define (D2 = lim_{r->0} d log C(r) / d log r, read off the linear stretch of the log-log correlation integral), and on fresh simulations it reproduces their published constants: RK4 Lorenz 2.0659 against 2.05 +- 0.01 (+0.77%) and Henon 1.2139 against 1.21 +- 0.01 (+0.32%, inside the interval). It resolves dimension at the SHIPPED N = 100: uniform d-cubes over 40 seeds give medians 1.9246 / 2.8981 / 4.2876 / 6.4377 / 8.6368 at d = 2/3/5/8/12 with 0/40 censored, while iid Gaussian in d = 768 and 4096 is correctly refused as `at_resolution_ceiling` at slopes 141.6 / 111.9 / 262.8. Both of the round-4 codex RED items are closed on this code state. (1) The cdist cancellation is gone: on its own float32 pair [0.001, 0.5, 0.75] vs [0.0010000100117, 0.5, 0.75] the task's exact path (H.double() then cdist with compute_mode='donot_use_mm_for_euclid_dist') returns 1.0011717677116394e-08, bit-equal to the stored separation, so no false zero and no spurious atomic verdict. (2) Its 3%-line/97%-cube mixture (analytic D2 = 1) is a SAMPLE-SIZE property of the GP estimator, not an implementation error: BLME returns 2.5920 at N = 5000 but 1.0094 at N = 20000, i.e. it converges to the analytic limit, and at p = 0.10 and 0.30 it already returns 1.0006 and 1.0076 at N = 5000. On the very cloud codex used, skdim's CorrInt -- the standard third-party GP implementation -- returns 2.8120, further from 1 than BLME's 2.5920.
comparable_reason: At the shipped configuration (num_samples = 100, pooling = mean, so N = 100 points) the estimate carries a sampling spread of the same order as the whole between-model range. Forty 100-of-400 document draws per model give sd 1.3417 (gpt2), 1.3201 (distilgpt2), 1.5159 (pythia-70m) and 1.6443 (pythia-160m) around means 6.86 / 8.13 / 9.77 / 8.53 -- a 15-19% coefficient of variation, 0/40 censored -- against a shipped four-model spread of 4.6051 to 7.4572. Point-count dependence is real but much smaller than codex reported on the round-4 build: going N = 100 -> 400 on the same corpus moves gpt2 6.8556 -> 7.1524 (+4.3%), distilgpt2 8.1270 -> 8.5580 (+5.3%), pythia-70m 9.7699 -> 8.9025 (-8.9%) and pythia-160m 8.5302 -> 7.8303 (-8.2%), where codex measured +20.0% to +73.2%; I could not reproduce that magnitude. So the cross-model ORDERING is not resolved at N = 100, which is a protocol problem rather than an estimator one -- the estimator itself is validated at that N against d-cubes above. A second, larger comparability lever is undisclosed: the task reads `out.hidden_states[-1]`, which is `ln_f(block L-1)`, so the cloud is a LayerNorm output rather than the deepest block's residual state. Substituting the block output (a `layers[-1]` forward hook) at the shipped protocol moves gpt2 5.4108 -> 4.4125 (-18.5%) and pythia-70m 5.2901 -> 7.8446 (+48.3%) -- the shift REVERSES SIGN between models and REVERSES THEIR ORDER (shipped gpt2 > pythia-70m; block-output pythia-70m > gpt2). This matches the convention geometry_lid uses for the same 'last layer' cloud, so it is consistent within the LID family, but nothing in the output records which state was measured.
github_reason: Grassberger & Procaccia (1983) released no code -- the papers predate software distribution and no authors' repository exists. The available cross-checks are later third-party implementations, and I ran one: skdim 0.3.4's `CorrInt` on uniform d-cubes at N = 2000 agrees with BLME to 3.25% / 4.09% / 1.42% / 3.68% at d = 2/3/5/8 (BLME 2.0110 / 2.9377 / 4.5543 / 6.9190 against 1.9478 / 2.8224 / 4.4906 / 6.6735), with BLME the higher and therefore the less negatively biased of the two at every d. On the adversarial low-mass mixture BLME is also the closer to the analytic answer (2.5920 vs skdim 2.8120 against a truth of 1).
paper_reason: Two of Grassberger & Procaccia's three published constants reproduce on fresh simulations: Lorenz D2 = 2.0659 against their 2.05 +- 0.01 (+0.77%, 0.006 above the stated upper bound) and Henon D2 = 1.2139 against 1.21 +- 0.01 (+0.32%, inside the interval). The third does NOT reproduce in my hands and the ledger's claim should be corrected: the logistic map at the Feigenbaum accumulation point reads 0.5311 (N = 5000) and 0.5285 (N = 20000, transient 200,000, r = 3.5699456718695445) against a published 0.500 +- 0.005, i.e. +5.7% to +6.2% and outside the interval, where RERUN_LEDGER.md Round 36 records 0.5005 (+0.11%). The saturation property also holds: Lorenz delay embeddings at m = 3/4/5 give 1.8566 / 1.9573 / 2.0218, converging on the state-space value rather than growing with embedding dimension.
confounds_reason: There is no MECHANICAL width dependence: the correlation integral is a function of pairwise distances only, so an isometric embedding of the same cloud into a wider space leaves it unchanged (codex measured 2.87e-12 across ambient widths 3 to 512, and I confirm the estimator depends on the distance vector alone). What the estimator IS mechanically bound to is the point count, which is a protocol constant here (N = 100 for every model), so it cannot separate models. Across the four locally permitted checkpoints at the shipped config the values are 5.4108 (gpt2) / 5.9919 (distilgpt2) / 7.4572 (pythia-70m) / 4.6051 (pythia-160m) with Spearman -0.775 against d_model (p = 0.225), -0.894 against n_layers (p = 0.106) and 0.000 against vocab size. With n = 4 and a per-model sampling sd of 1.32-1.64, none of these is distinguishable from noise -- hence SUSPECTED rather than CONFIRMED.
defects: CODE/CONFIG WIRING, correlation_dimension.py:87 and the two `_gp_correlation_dimension_plateau(distances)` calls: the configured `num_radii` (defaults.yaml:45, num_radii = 30) reaches ONLY the demoted percentile helper. I verified the headline is bit-identical at 3.1338888100 for num_radii = 10/30/60/100/300 while the demoted key moves 2.1186 -> 2.1478 -- and the primary is materially sensitive to that grid when it is actually passed: plateau(num_radii = 10/30/60/100/300) on the same 3-cube gives 2.6187 / 2.2945 / 3.1339 / 3.5939 / 3.4422, a 37% spread. A shipped knob that is silently inert on the headline should either be wired through (and then re-validated) or removed from defaults.yaml.

DISCLOSURE (CODE), correlation_dimension.py:110 `last_hidden = out.hidden_states[-1][0]`: this is `ln_f(block L-1)`, a LayerNorm output, not the deepest block's residual state, and no `_meta_last_entry_is_block_output` flag is emitted (the nine tasks this campaign rewired all emit one). LayerNorm projects every row onto a fixed-radius shell, and a correlation dimension is a purely geometric statistic, so the choice matters: substituting the true block output moves gpt2 5.4108 -> 4.4125 (-18.5%) and pythia-70m 5.2901 -> 7.8446 (+48.3%) and REVERSES the two models' ordering. Consistent with geometry_lid's convention for the same cloud, so I do not score it as a fidelity defect -- but it is undisclosed and model-dependent, so it should carry a provenance flag.

CODE, correlation_dimension.py:_ATOM_PAIR_FRAC_MIN = 0.0025 is NOT resolution-aware. At the shipped N = 100 the threshold is defensible and I would keep it: 0.0025 of 4,950 pairs is 12.4 pairs against the plateau grid's own 10-pair counting floor (10/4950 = 0.00202), so the gate fires almost exactly when an atom becomes resolvable, and the three calibration cases behave as documented (1 duplicate row in 100 -> c0 = 0.00020202, does not fire; a 10% point mass -> 0.00909091, fires; 23 coincident of 100 -> 0.05111111, fires). But the same constant is 500x the counting floor at N = 2000 (10/1,999,000 = 5.0e-06), so a genuinely resolvable atom is missed there: a 4% point mass (80 of 2000 coincident, c0 = 0.001581, 3,160 coincident pairs) does NOT fire and the reported continuous fit reads 2.3303 against 2.8898 for the same cloud without the atom (-19.4%), where the GP limit is exactly 0. Latent on real data -- `_meta_correlation_dimension_zero_pair_frac` is 0.0 on all four models at defaults -- but the threshold should scale as max(k, 10)/n_pairs, not be a constant.

AUDIT-TRAIL, correlation_dimension.py:360 and 490: `_meta_correlation_dimension_eckmann_ruelle_slope_bound` is still emitted (4.0 at N = 100) beside headline values of 4.6051-7.4572 that carry status `ok`, so the emitted bound contradicts the emitted decision. My d-cube calibration shows the bound is empirically wrong for this estimator's small-radius window (it recovers d = 8 at 6.44 and d = 12 at 8.64 from N = 100), so the key should be dropped rather than left as a number a reader will read as a validity limit. `d2_ceiling` is likewise computed inside the plateau helper and never used -- the same dead-assignment pattern flagged elsewhere in this campaign.

PROTOCOL/COMPARABILITY, defaults.yaml:42-47: num_samples = 100 with pooling = 'mean' gives N = 100 points, and `max_points: 2000` cannot raise it because mean pooling yields one point per document. Forty draws per model give sd 1.32-1.64 against a four-model range of 2.85, so the shipped configuration does not resolve the cross-model ordering.

BOUNDARY (trivial), correlation_dimension.py: the pair floor uses `C > 10/total` where the comment says a radius is usable 'once it contains enough pairs' (i.e. >=). On a 100-point 3-cube that excludes 3 of 39 otherwise-usable radii.
fix: Wire the configured `num_radii` into both `_gp_correlation_dimension_plateau` calls or delete it from defaults.yaml -- as shipped it is inert on the headline while the headline moves 37% across the range it names. Make `_ATOM_PAIR_FRAC_MIN` resolution-scaled (e.g. max(10, 12)/n_pairs) so the atomic rule keeps its shipped-N calibration while still firing on a resolvable atom at larger N; the measured cost of the constant is a -19.4% bias on a 4% point mass at N = 2000. Drop `_meta_correlation_dimension_eckmann_ruelle_slope_bound` and the unused `d2_ceiling`, since the d-cube calibration refutes the bound for this window. Raise the effective point count (or report the bootstrap sd, which the task already has the machinery for) before the value is used to order models. Finally, correct RERUN_LEDGER.md's logistic-map claim from 0.5005 to the reproducible 0.529-0.531. Emit a provenance flag for the point cloud (`_meta_last_entry_is_block_output`) since the post-ln_f vs deepest-block choice is worth -18.5% on gpt2 and +48.3% on pythia-70m and reverses their order.
